title: Whether a method can be both private and protected
answer: No. A Java member cannot be declared with two conflicting access modifiers such as `private protected`. Access modifiers are mutually exclusive: a member is `public`, `protected`, package-private, or `private`. `private` restricts access to the declaring top-level class and nestmates, while `protected` permits broader package and subclass access. Choose the narrowest visibility that matches the API contract rather than combining modifiers.
